compiled_state.title: [aws-setup-lambda.sh]: Function URL AUTH=NONE blocked by AWS Organization SCP -> public POST returns 403
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## 1. Technical Environment
code_version: 0ea7a48e8677fee18aa65c99092dbba27d8e88df

## 2. Incident Overview
Scenario Type: Sub-Agent Blocker (informational)

### Expected
With AuthType=NONE and lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl permission attached to principal '*', anonymous curl POST to Function URL returns 2xx response.

### Actual
Anonymous POST returns 403 'AccessDeniedException' even after adding the public-invoke permission. SigV4-signed POST with AUTH=AWS_IAM also returns 403. Account is in AWS Organization o-t5fn7az6cp (CONSOLIDATED_BILLING) — likely org SCP denying public Function URL access.

Underlying telemetry pipeline (direct Lambda invoke → S3 → schema validation) works end-to-end (StatusCode 202, object lands, schema validates ok=True).

### Suggested fix
Either: (a) document that Function URL AUTH=NONE requires the AWS account to NOT have an org SCP denying Lambda public access — add a preflight check; (b) change design to AUTH=AWS_IAM with documented authenticated client emission path; (c) document the SCP requirement in INSTALL.md.

Priority 3 — does not block telemetry-pipeline operation (direct invocation works); affects the documented integration path for review-emit dispatcher.
